## ✨ Added

- **Branding app, optional.** A new **Branding admin app** toggle (`BRANDING_APP`, advanced view) adds a **Branding** entry to the OpenCloud app menu. Admins can set the instance name and slogan, a logo for light and dark mode, the favicon, the login background, and whether the sign-in card is light, dark, or follows the visitor's browser. Until now that meant editing `theme.json` in the data folder by hand. Only accounts with the `Logo.Write` permission see the entry, which by default means admins, and the service behind it asks OpenCloud about every change. Off by default, so existing installs are unaffected. Saved changes take effect without a restart; only flipping the toggle needs one.
- **Login page follows your branding.** OpenCloud's sign-in page reads only the logo from the theme, so the image ships OpenCloud's own page with one added script line, installed through `IDP_ASSET_PATH`. The page then shows your name in the tab title, your name and slogan in the footer, your background and your favicon, and the card in the look you picked. With nothing saved it stays byte-identical to OpenCloud's own page. If you set `IDP_ASSET_PATH` yourself, the wrapper leaves it alone.
- **Uploads by clicking the preview.** Each image section shows what the instance really uses, on the top bar colour of its own theme. Clicking the preview opens the file chooser; the menu beside it resets the image to the OpenCloud default. PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG are accepted, up to 5 MB per logo, 2 MB for the favicon and 25 MB for the background. SVG files are rebuilt from an allowlist of shapes and attributes, so nothing that could run code or freeze the browser survives.
- **Test images for feature branches.** A push to a branch now builds `ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/opencloud:<branch>` and `:<branch>-rolling`, so a change can be tried on a real server before it is merged. `latest`, `production`, `rolling`, the version tags and the Docker Hub mirror stay reserved for `main` and release tags.

## ⚡ Improved

- README gained a **Branding** section covering the toggle, the fields, the SVG rules, the login page, what happens when you switch the app back off, and how to add the `/brandingsvc/` route to a `proxy.yaml` of your own.
- CI covers the branding app on both channels. It lints, type checks and tests the Go service and the web extension, then boots each built image with the app on and with it off, checking the theme against the server, the refusals, the uploads and the sign-in page.
